subject: Clarify notice anchoring, grace limits, and early-exit fee tiers
messages:
From: HarborHealth <procurement@harborhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Linda Choi <linda.choi@hawthornlegal.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOW & Term alignment — notice windows, opt-out, and early-exit fees

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Our procurement team is reviewing the MSA + Order Form and we have a few timing questions before legal finalizes the signature. Narrow asks below so we can get internal sign-off: 

- Order form currently says 60-day written notice to opt out of auto-renew. We were hoping for a 45-day window tied to the invoice cycle. Any flexibility?
- If HarborHealth exercises early termination for convenience (post-commitment), we need clarity on how support/transition is billed. Are you proposing pro-rata only, or do you have a fee ladder for early off-ramps?
- Related: if the Term alignment is anchored to the subscription billing cycle (monthly vs. annual), what happens if notice falls inside a billing period — do you prorate to month-end?

We can accept a modest termination fee if it reduces the notice window, but need the math up-front. Can you provide a short summary and the redline language your legal team prefers? If possible, attach a redline we can circulate.

Appreciate it — procurement would like to close this week if the language is straightforward.

Best,
Alex Ramirez
Sr. Manager, Procurement
HarborHealth
[Attachment: Harbor_HarborHealth_RFP_June2025.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: HarborHealth <procurement@harborhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOW & Term alignment — notice windows, opt-out, and early-exit fees

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses here and next steps below. I've attached a one-page summary for your legal and procurement teams.

Short answers:
- Notice window: we can move to a 45-day written notice (from the current 60) if the termination-for-convenience fee is tiered (see fee ladder below). The 45 days would be measured from the end of the then-current Term and can be tied to the billing cycle so you don't lose an entire invoice period when notice falls mid-cycle.
- Billing on early exit: standard approach is pro-rata for unused days plus a termination-for-convenience fee if exit is inside the first 180 days of a Term.
- Fee ladder (proposal):
  - Exit inside 0–90 days of Term start: 50% of remaining Term fees
  - Exit 91–180 days: 25% of remaining Term fees
  - Exit after 180 days: pro-rata only

Proposed redline language (summary):
"The Order Form shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month Terms unless either party provides written notice no later than forty-five (45) days prior to the end of the then-current Term. If Customer terminates for convenience prior to one hundred eighty (180) days after the start of a Term, Customer shall pay the fees set forth in the Order Form as an early termination fee per the schedule below in addition to any unpaid, pro-rata fees."

Next steps (action items):
- Neha: can you review the one-pager and confirm whether the proposed ladder and the 45-day anchor are OK from a legal/risk perspective?
- Ben: please confirm ops impact (SLA + capacity planning) and any required handoff window if HarborHealth chooses a mid-month off-ramp.
- Alex: if this looks acceptable we can produce a redline (pdf) and a clean amendment for signature (DocuSign link to follow).

Attachment: [Attachment: Marissa_Response_Summary_20250712.txt (txt)]

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Office: +1 (415) 555-0116

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOW & Term alignment — notice windows, opt-out, and early-exit fees

Marissa / Neha — quick ops read: we're comfortable with a 45-day notice so long as we define the handoff window for support/transition and protect capacity commitments. A few operational clarifications: 

- If notice falls mid-billing period, we should offer pro-rata to month-end rather than day-by-day to avoid fractional billing and excessive billing noise. That matches most enterprise buyers.
- For the 0–90 day 50% ladder: that will require reserving capacity until the end of the notice window if the customer requests active handoff support. Suggest adding explicit language that professional services (onboarding/custom integrations) costs are not subject to pro-rata refund — that protects PS spend.

I can draft a brief ops addendum sentence: "Professional services fees are non-refundable; subscription fees will be prorated to the end of the then-current billing period unless otherwise specified."

No blockers from my side — happy to join the call if Procurement wants to lock this down.

— Ben
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: HarborHealth <procurement@harborhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Jul 2025 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOW & Term alignment — notice windows, opt-out, and early-exit fees

Alex / Marissa / Ben — looping in formal legal response and a clean redline attached. We can accept the 45-day notice anchored to the end of the then-current Term with the fee ladder proposed by Marissa, subject to the clarifications below: 

1) Anchor and measurement: The 45-day notice will be measured from the last day of the then-current Term. If Customer provides notice after the start of the final month of a Term, the parties will treat the effective termination date as the end of the billing cycle and apply pro-rata to month-end unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.

2) Fee ladder: We will incorporate the ladder as proposed (50% / 25% / pro-rata) but add a cap: early termination fees shall not exceed the aggregate remaining subscription fees for the then-current Term.

3) PS carveout: We will add explicit language excluding professional services and third-party pass-through costs from refunds.

4) Compliance/Security hold: For customers under SOC 2 or specific audit requirements (HarborHealth noted their healthcare posture), Redwood may hold exported logs and a final export window of up to 30 days after termination; we will include standard data-export assistance language and a reference to our data handling addendum.

I attached two files: a redline PDF of the Order Form and a one-page amendment that matches the billing/proration approach. If HarborHealth agrees to the cap and the PS carveout, we can issue a DocuSign amendment by Monday.
